notes.title: Free-to-Play Announcement
notes.notes:
Hey there!

I’ve decided to switch [i]Pierrot à la Mode[/i] to Free to Play, and I wanted to talk about why that is in case anybody is curious.

Originally, my research told me that free games / demos on Steam don’t translate well to paid sales further down the line, and as this game is essentially a prequel to[i] Gas Station Story[/i] (which will be a paid product), I figured it should at least have a small price tag so people aren’t surprised when GSS releases. I also was hoping to gather some funds that would aid me in completing GSS, as I need to commission more music for the final release, as well as pay for things like code signing so I can distribute the Windows app outside of Steam. 

However, I’ve noticed that there are a disproportionate amount of wishlists to purchases (not to mention itch.io, which has had 0 sales), even when the game goes on sale to 50% off. I think I may have screwed up my evaluation of how much this 15-20 minute game was worth. I was hoping the $1.99 price tag would allow the game to still be accessible to interested parties, but that doesn’t seem to be the case. Which is fair! There are hundreds of games out there that are cheaper or free and offer dozens of hours of replayability, versus the 20-30 minutes you might get out of [i]Pierrot à la Mode[/i] (x3 endings). And even in comparison to [i]Gas Station Story[/i], which runs about 4-6 hours per playthrough (x26 endings), that $1.99 for a half hour doesn’t match with whatI’m expecting to price [i]Gas Station Story[/i] at.

So! I’ve decided to switch [i]Pierrot à la Mode[/i] to Free to Play, so that more people can have access to this short story and, hopefully, raise more awareness for Gas Station Story as well. As of right now, after roughly half a year of being live, I haven’t even sold enough copies to even cover the cost of listing the game on Steam, so I’m releasing it into the FtP realm to be enjoyed by whomever stumbles upon it. Alongside this, I’ll be archiving the 1.0 version into the ether (my hard drive) as 1.1 will be the new web player version.

Thanks for reading, and if you’re one of the [redacted] people that bought PalM before this switch, shoot me an email or hit me up [url=https://www.instagram.com/issumatek/]@issumatek[/url] on instagram to chat! I would be happy to offer a refund to anybody that feels slighted by this switch. One way or the other, I’ll update this page later this year (much later…) with a final lookback and potentially some new content. 

A quick plug here because I gotta - the Kickstarter campaign for [i]Gas Station Story[/i] will be launching in one month! Give it a pre-save at the [url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/issumatek/gas-station-story-a-surreal-sci-fi-slice-of-life]link here,[/url] or if you’re reading this after February 25nd, give it a pledge if you can! I would really appreciate your support if you’re able to give it - some of the costs associated with officially launching the beast that is [i]Gas Station Story[/i] are a little too high for me right now!

Love,
Enzi

notes.title: Pierrot á la Mode is Now Available!
notes.notes:
Hello there!

Welcome to the Steam page for my first (completed) project, [i]Pierrot à la Mode[/i]. I originally made this game in 2023 for the [b]Big Mode Game Jam[/b], and completed the first version of the game within the span of two weeks.

This game uses photos taken with the [b]Game Boy Camera[/b] for each level’s title card and for every character portrait during dialogue sequences. The photos were originally in 4-tone green, like the first Game Boy, with color added after the fact in GB Studio. However, all of the character effects are practical! I purchased clown makeup and the noses, and reused a couple of masks that I bought during the production of [i]Gas Station Story[/i]. Beyond removing the backgrounds each character was photographed in, the pixels are straight from the GB Cam.

Speaking of, [i]Pierrot à la Mode[/i] is meant to serve as a sort of prequel to the events of [i]Gas Station Story[/i], a similarly styled project I’ve been working on for a couple of years now. Thematically, the games don’t share much beyond having the same Point-of-Sale system (hint hint) and touching on the woes of working in customer service. 

The new build of the game includes a revitalized [b]Clown Mode[/b] that functions as I originally envisioned, as well as numerous bugfixes and a new ending variation if you achieve a perfect score -- this new ending will give you a bit of a hint towards what's coming in the back half of [i]Gas Station Story[/i]. Good luck at pulling off a perfect score! I struggle with it myself. I’m working on a way to have this Steam version save between levels, but haven’t quite cracked it yet. 

Some day I'll be returning to this project to show you what happens to the Dairy Clown crew after that new special ending, but that's a story for another time. In the meantime, I’ll be continuing development on [i]Gas Station Story[/i] and trying to figure out why the Electron Wrapper doesn’t like my .sav files. Thanks so much for playing! 



[b]Changelog (V1.1 - PC)[/b]

Global:

- Electron wrapper completed

- Performance enhancements

- Color swapping slowed down (background palettes change between 4 colors in 3 seconds)

- PC version now has appropriate button instructions (A=Z, D-Pad=WASD/Arrow Keys, Start=Enter, Select=Left Shift)

- Added “Perfect Score” ending variation


Toppings:

- Topping Boxes now look like boxes

- Topping Selector code rewritten to be more stable

- Added Shift Key function (to reset topping selector location)

- Conveyor belt variable speeds fixed (starts running when you can top the ice-cream, stops when checking orders, goes faster during Clown Mode)

- Clown Mode now reverses toppings when activated



Order Sheet:

- Changed “Order XX” to “#XX”

- Removed dashes and numbers

- Changed “Great Work!” to “Yes!”

- Numerous text glitches fixed
